{{Short description|Russian and American theoretical physicist (1953–2020)}}
'''Mikhail "Misha" Voloshin''' (May 14, 1953, [[Bucharest]], Romania – March 20, 2020)<ref>[https://cse.umn.edu/physics/news/mikhail-misha-voloshin-1953-2020 University of Minnesota: In Memoriam, Mikhail Voloshin]</ref> was a Russian and American [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]]. Voloshin graduated from physics class of [[Moscow State School 57]] in 1970. Voloshin started working at [[Institute for Theoretical and Experimental Physics|ITEP]] in 1976 and accordingly earned his Ph.D. in 1977. In 1983 he received a Soviet medal and an award in physics. Beginning in 1990, he taught quantum physics at the [[William I Fine Theoretical Physics Institute, University of Minnesota|William I Fine Theoretical Physics Institute]], a division of the [[University of Minnesota College of Science and Engineering]]. In 1997 elected a [[fellow]] of the [[American Physical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=American Physical Society|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=1997&unit_id=&institution=University+of+Minnesota}} (search on year=1997 and institution=University of Minnesota)</ref> In 2001 he was awarded [[Sakurai Prize|J.J. Sakurai Prize for Theoretical Particle Physics]]<ref>{{cite web|url= http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?last_nm=Voloshin&first_nm=Mikhail&year=2001|title=Mikhail Voloshin|publisher= APS|accessdate=September 18, 2013}}</ref> and in 2004 he was awarded the [[Humboldt Prize|Alexander-von-Humboldt Award]].<ref>[https://www.physics.umn.edu/about/news/general/13282/In_Memoriam_Mikhail_Voloshin In Memoriam University of Minnesota] Retrieved February 14, 2014.</ref>
